items.title: Galerkin coarse matrices and the exact coarse-correction error map
items.statement: Let $A_h\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite and let $P\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ have full column rank, with $1\le m\le n$. Define the Galerkin coarse matrix $A_H:=P^{\mathsf T}A_hP$. Whenever $A_H$ is invertible, define the exact coarse-correction error map $C:=I_n-PA_H^{-1}P^{\mathsf T}A_h$. Here $P$ prolongs coarse coordinates to fine coordinates and $P^{\mathsf T}$ restricts fine residuals. The definition is in exact real arithmetic; it does not identify a rediscretized coarse operator with $A_H$.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods
Numerical Methods II, University of Heidelberg lecture notes, Chapter 10: Multigrid Methods

items.title: Continuous piecewise-affine functions with zero endpoints lie in H1-zero
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Every continuous real function on $[0,1]$ that is affine on the intervals of a finite partition and vanishes at both endpoints belongs to $H^1_0(0,1)$, defined as the $W^{1,2}$-norm closure of $C_c^\infty(0,1)$.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods
Numerical Methods II, University of Heidelberg lecture notes, Chapter 10: Multigrid Methods

items.strategy: Direct cutoff, zero-extension, and mollification proof with explicit Sobolev closure argument.

items.title: The Galerkin coarse correction is an energy-orthogonal projector
items.statement: For $A_h$ symmetric positive definite and $P$ full column rank as in [[def-galerkin-coarse-grid-correction]], the Galerkin matrix $A_H=P^{\mathsf T}A_hP$ is symmetric positive definite, so the coarse-correction map $C$ is defined. It satisfies $C^2=C$, $CP=0$, $P^{\mathsf T}A_hC=0$, and $C^{\mathsf T}A_h=A_hC$. Hence its range is the $A_h$-orthogonal complement of $\operatorname{Ran}(P)$, and $C$ is the orthogonal projection onto that complement for $\langle x,y\rangle_{A_h}=x^{\mathsf T}A_hy$.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods
Numerical Methods II, University of Heidelberg lecture notes, Chapter 10: Multigrid Methods

items.strategy: Direct algebraic proof with explicit hypotheses and boundary checks.

items.title: The symmetric two-grid error map from a pre-smoother and Galerkin correction
items.statement: Let $A_h$ be symmetric positive definite, let $C$ be the exact Galerkin error projector of [[thm-galerkin-coarse-correction-is-energy-orthogonal-projector]], and let $S$ be a linear pre-smoothing error map. Its $A_h$-adjoint is $S^{*_{A_h}}:=A_h^{-1}S^{\mathsf T}A_h$. The symmetric two-grid error map is $E:=S^{*_{A_h}}CS$: it applies pre-smoothing, exact coarse correction, then the $A_h$-adjoint post-smoother.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods
Numerical Methods II, University of Heidelberg lecture notes, Chapter 10: Multigrid Methods

items.title: Finite strength-graph aggregation and Galerkin hierarchy with explicit statuses
items.statement:
Input an integer $n_0\ge1$ and a real symmetric positive-definite matrix $A_0\in\mathbb R^{n_0	imes n_0}$ with nonpositive off-diagonal entries, a strength threshold $0<	heta<1$, a coarse-size threshold $n_{\min}\ge1$, and a level cap $L\ge0$. At each level $\ell<L$ with $n_\ell>n_{\min}$, form an undirected graph on $\{1,\ldots,n_\ell\}$: join $i
e j$ when $a_{ij}^{(\ell)}<0$ and either $-a_{ij}^{(\ell)}\ge	heta\max_{k
e i}(-a_{ik}^{(\ell)})$ or $-a_{ij}^{(\ell)}\ge	heta\max_{k
e j}(-a_{jk}^{(\ell)})$. Repeatedly take the smallest still-unassigned vertex $i$ and make one aggregate from $i$ and all its still-unassigned graph neighbours; remove that nonempty aggregate and continue. Set $(P_\ell)_{ic}=1$ when fine index $i$ belongs to aggregate $c$ and $0$ otherwise. If the aggregate count is not smaller than $n_\ell$, return status `coarsening-stalled`. Otherwise set $A_{\ell+1}=P_\ell^{\mathsf T}A_\ell P_\ell$ and continue. Return `coarse-reached` when $n_\ell\le n_{\min}$, `level-cap` when the cap is reached first, or `coarsening-stalled` on a nonreducing step, together with all completed matrices and prolongations. This setup procedure makes no convergence claim.

references.title: Chen-Song Zhang, Multilevel Iterative Methods, version 0.5, Chapter 6: Multigrid Methods
Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods

items.strategy: Finite explicit setup/recursion with bounded status branches; no convergence claim is included.

items.title: Level-uniform 1D Poisson smoothing and approximation bounds
items.statement:
Let $N=2M\ge4$, $h=1/N$, and $A_h=h^{-1}\operatorname{tridiag}(-1,2,-1)$ on the $N-1$ interior nodes of the uniform Dirichlet mesh of $(0,1)$. Let $P$ be piecewise-linear interpolation from the $M-1$ interior coarse nodes at even fine indices, $A_H=P^{\mathsf T}A_hP$, $C=I-PA_H^{-1}P^{\mathsf T}A_h$, and $S=I-A_h/\lambda_{\max}(A_h)$. For every integer $
u\ge1$ and fine error $e$, $\|CS^
u e\|_{A_h}^2\le rac{2}{2
u+1}\|e\|_{A_h}^2$. In particular, the joint smoothing-correction constant $ho=2/(2
u+1)$ is less than $1$ and is independent of $N$.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods
Numerical Methods II, University of Heidelberg lecture notes, Chapter 10: Multigrid Methods

items.title: Finite recursive Galerkin V- and W-cycle for an SPD hierarchy
items.statement:
Input a finite Galerkin hierarchy of real SPD matrices $A_j\in\mathbb R^{n_j	imes n_j}$ with $n_j\ge1$ and full-column-rank prolongations $P_j\in\mathbb R^{n_j	imes n_{j-1}}$ satisfying $A_{j-1}=P_j^{\mathsf T}A_jP_j$. For an invocation at level $j$, take $x,b\in\mathbb R^{n_j}$, nonnegative sweep counts $
u_1,
u_2$, positive integer $\gamma$, and pre/post residual-correction matrices $K_j^{\mathrm{pre}},K_j^{\mathrm{post}}\in\mathbb R^{n_j	imes n_j}$. Define $\mathrm{Cycle}(0,x,b)=A_0^{-1}b$. For $j>0$, pre-smooth $x$ by $
u_1$ steps, set $r=b-A_jx$ and $e=0$, then for $t=1,\ldots,\gamma$ set $e\leftarrow\mathrm{Cycle}(j-1,e,P_j^{\mathsf T}r)$. Correct $x\leftarrow x+P_je$, post-smooth $
u_2$ steps, and return $x$. The V-cycle is $\gamma=1$ and the W-cycle is $\gamma=2$. Setup cost, floating-point error, and convergence are separate claims.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods
Numerical Methods II, University of Heidelberg lecture notes, Chapter 10: Multigrid Methods

items.title: A joint smoothing-correction estimate gives symmetric two-grid energy contraction
items.statement: Let $A_h$, $C$, $S$, and $E=S^{*_{A_h}}CS$ be as in [[def-symmetric-two-grid-error-operator]]. If $0\le\rho<1$ and $\|CSx\|_{A_h}^2\le\rho\|x\|_{A_h}^2$ for every fine-grid vector $x$, then $E$ is self-adjoint and nonnegative in the $A_h$ inner product and its induced operator norm satisfies $\|E\|_{A_h}\le\rho$. The hypothesis is the joint estimate; separate smoothing and approximation inequalities imply it only when their compatibility is proved.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods
Numerical Methods II, University of Heidelberg lecture notes, Chapter 10: Multigrid Methods

items.title: Finite aggregation AMG preserves the SPD matrix class and returns a status
items.statement: For every admissible input to [[alg-aggregation-based-algebraic-multigrid-hierarchy]], every successful aggregate partition covers the current indices by nonempty disjoint sets. Its indicator prolongation has full column rank. Each successful Galerkin product $A_{\ell+1}=P_\ell^{\mathsf T}A_\ell P_\ell$ is symmetric positive definite with nonpositive off-diagonal entries. The procedure terminates after at most $L$ coarsening attempts and returns exactly one of `coarse-reached`, `level-cap`, or `coarsening-stalled`; none of these statuses implies multigrid convergence.

references.title: Chen-Song Zhang, Multilevel Iterative Methods, version 0.5, Chapter 6: Multigrid Methods
Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods

items.title: Work recurrence for fixed-coarsening multigrid cycles in all three regimes
items.statement: Suppose each level with $N$ unknowns has $cN$ work outside recursion, the next level has $N/q$ unknowns for fixed $q=2^d>1$, the base solve has bounded cost, and each cycle makes $\gamma\ge1$ recursive calls. Then $T(N)=cN+\gamma T(N/q)$ has order $\Theta(N)$ if $\gamma<q$, $\Theta(N\log N)$ if $\gamma=q$, and $\Theta(N^{\log_q\gamma})$ if $\gamma>q$. These are arithmetic-work bounds conditional on the stated uniform per-level cost and coarsening assumptions; they do not imply convergence.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods

items.title: The symmetric 1D Poisson two-grid cycle is uniformly contractive
items.statement:
For the one-dimensional nested-grid data of [[lem-one-dimensional-poisson-smoothing-and-approximation]], take $S_{\mathrm{pre}}=S^
u$ and the $A_h$-adjoint post-smoother. Then the joint estimate holds with $ho=2/(2
u+1)$, and the symmetric two-grid error operator satisfies $\|E\|_{A_h}\le2/(2
u+1)\le2/3$ for every $N=2M\ge4$ and every $
u\ge1$.

items.title: A linear error on the one-dimensional Poisson coarse space is removed exactly
items.statement: For the piecewise-linear finite-element discretization of the homogeneous Dirichlet Poisson form on $(0,1)$ with $N=4$ fine intervals, the interior error vector $e=(1,2,1)^{\mathsf T}$ is the prolongation of the single coarse interior value $2$. The exact Galerkin coarse correction therefore sends $e$ to $0$.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods
Numerical Methods II, University of Heidelberg lecture notes, Chapter 10: Multigrid Methods

items.title: V- and W-cycle work under two-dimensional four-to-one coarsening
items.statement: Let $N=4^L$ with integer $L\ge1$, assume linear work per level and a four-to-one reduction in level size, and take V-cycle $\gamma=1$ and W-cycle $\gamma=2$. Both cycles have $\Theta(N)$ arithmetic work, with per-level recursion ratios $1/4$ and $1/2$ respectively.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods
Numerical Methods II, University of Heidelberg lecture notes, Chapter 10: Multigrid Methods

items.title: One high-frequency mode in the finite one-dimensional Poisson two-grid cycle
items.statement: For every nested uniform Dirichlet grid with $N=2M\ge4$ intervals, the stiffness matrix $h^{-1}\operatorname{tridiag}(-1,2,-1)$, piecewise-linear coarse interpolation, exact Galerkin correction, and $\nu\ge1$ Richardson sweeps with step $1/\lambda_{\max}(A_h)$ have the symmetric two-grid energy contraction factor at most $2/(2\nu+1)$.

references.title: Susanne C. Brenner and L. Ridgway Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, 3rd ed., Chapter 6: Finite Element Multigrid Methods
Numerical Methods II, University of Heidelberg lecture notes, Chapter 10: Multigrid Methods
